messages:
jess: FYI ACME prod reporting a bunch of 429s + spikes in p50/p95 latency starting ~11:40 UTC. Customer says their UX times out. Tenant: acme-prod. Route: POST /v1/completions (model: redwood/open-7b-q4).

leo: grabbing traces and request ids now. do we have a tenant-level quota breach or a route quirk?

maya: alert fired on `limits.overage` at 11:42, I see a correlated surge in requests per second for that tenant. Dashboard: https://console.redwood.internal/d/limits/tenants — filter acme-prod.

srebot: Incident bot: RateLimitAlarm -> tenant=acme-prod, rule=tenant_request_rate, threshold=5000rps, value=7321rps, window=1m.

leo: can you paste a few sample request_ids so I can trace?

jess: request_ids: rq_1a2b3c, rq_1a2b3d, rq_1a2b3e. Also seeing many retry stamps in headers: `x-retry-count: 4`

maya: running a quick fingerprint query to attribute throttles by route/model/customer:
```
SELECT tenant_id, route, model, count(*) AS throttles
FROM telemetry.rate_limit_events
WHERE ts BETWEEN 1742004000 AND 1742006000
AND tenant_id = 'acme-prod'
GROUP BY tenant_id, route, model
ORDER BY throttles DESC
LIMIT 20;
```

maya: result: majority are on `/v1/completions` with model redwood/open-7b-q4 — 98% of 429s attributed to that combo.

leo: interesting — is it a sudden traffic spike from a new deploy or client change? any recent rollout to their org?

jess: they rolled out a frontend change at 11:30 that removed jitter/backoff on our client lib. Ticket from account: https://acme.atlassian.net/browse/ACME-314

oncall-sre: @leo @jess, provisional mitigation options: 1) apply temporary tenant burst increase (10% for 30m), 2) enable per-route short-circuit (reject heavier batch sizes), 3) ask customer to re-enable client backoff. Which first?

leo: do 1) to buy time and 3) as ask. Also schedule an alert refinement — current alert triggers on raw rps which flaps. We should alert on sustained error-rate > 5% over 3m.

maya: applied a soft quota bump via admin panel: tenant=acme-prod, +15% burst for 40m. watching metrics.

srebot: ChangeLog: soft-quota-bump by maya for tenant acme-prod (+15%, expires 1742008320).

jess: customer confirmed they re-enabled jitter/backoff. they pushed a hotfix at 11:55.

leo: tracing those request_ids now — I see retries creating a thundering herd. sample span: service=frontend -> client-retry -> gateway -> inference. Gateway queued tokens then hit rate limiter and returned 429.

maya: telemetry snippet: `throttle_count` went from ~20/min pre-11:40 to ~1800/min peak. Token bucket refill unchanged.

leo: root cause: client removed exponential backoff, causing exponential retry pileup at peak. Secondary: route capacity tuned for average batch size; sudden increase in concurrent small requests hurt p95.

jess: resolution for the customer: explain root cause, confirm client fix, and issue a temporary credit? billing-bot, any guidance on credits for outage?

billing-bot: Suggest credit: 2 days of burst overage fees waived; escalate to billing team for approval. Please open ticket with usage window + cost delta.

jess: will open a follow-up ticket and share step-by-step repro and telemetry.

leo: followups for platform:
- Add a tenant-level 'retry-fingerprint' metric that tracks requests with x-retry-count>=3 so we can alert earlier.
- Add an alert rule: sustained 5% 429s for a tenant over 3m.
- Add a per-route p95 latency heatmap to identify model-specific capacity pressure.

maya: created infra tickets: INF-1203 (retry-fingerprint metric), INF-1204 (alert rule), INF-1205 (route p95 heatmap).

jess: I'll hand off to support to coordinate customer comms + billing ticket.

oncall-sre: marking incident resolved for now — soft quota expired and traffic normalized after frontend fix. Closing notes: cause=client retries, mitigation=temporary burst, long-term=fingerprint metric + alerting. :white_check_mark:
